chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from Muhammad ibn Isa from Isma'il from Khirash from Zurarah said:
"Witnesses are not accepted if they are separate; if there are three, the fourth is accepted after them."

key_terms.مُتَفَرِّقِينَ: separate/scattered (acting individually rather than as a group)

ai.seo_question: What is the condition for the acceptance of witnesses when they are separate according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the procedural requirement for witness testimony (*bayyinah*), emphasizing that scattered or independent testimonies are not accepted as a single unit. It establishes that a group of three witnesses can validate the testimony of a fourth, ensuring the integrity and collective weight of the evidence in judicial proceedings. This ruling reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on the cohesion and reliability of witness groups to prevent fragmented or contradictory claims.
